key_insight: Wearable, minute-level temperature patterns plus machine learning can help distinguish engraftment fever from other fever causes in HCT patients.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support faster fever-etiology triage during hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, when diagnostic uncertainty is common.
method: 68 clinically independent fever episodes from 90 HCT patients were monitored with an FDA-cleared wearable temperature sensor every 2 minutes.
Time-series features were extracted from 1 hour before to 3 hours after fever onset.
Multiple machine-learning models were compared using repeated stratified 5-fold patient-level cross-validation.
evidence_signal: The best model was logistic regression, achieving 94% specificity for engraftment fevers and a mean AUROC of 0.88 across 100 train-test evaluations.
watch_item: The study is small and single-setting, so external validation is needed before real-world deployment.
paper_title: Rapid diagnosis of fever etiology using wearable temperature monitoring and machine learning
